broadcasts.message: normalize.js ready. NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to one space, trim. Non-string returns empty string. No word changes.

Implemented tokenize(text) per spec: calls injected normalize(text), extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes using regex, returns array in input order. Empty/non-matching input returns empty array. No stopwords or negation removal. Ready for integration.

pipeline.js implemented. processText calls injected tokenize(text) once, builds frequencies with Object.create(null) to safely handle tokens like 'constructor'. Returns exact shape: text joined by spaces, tokens array, count, unique in first-seen order, frequencies mapping. Ready for integration.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 1: normalize.js implemented. Spec: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. Do not alter words. Ready for review.
private_memories.tokenizer: Goal: implement tokenizer.js per spec. Round 1: initial implementation. Key decisions: use regex [A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*, call injected normalize(text). Ensure no shadowing. Future: verify with peers, handle edge cases.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: I am the integrator for pipeline.js. My module processText(text) must call injected tokenize(text) exactly once and return the specified object. Dependencies normalize and tokenize are injected; do not shadow. Must handle prototype keys (constructor) in frequencies. Use Object.create(null) for frequencies to avoid prototype pollution. Return text as tokens.join(' '). No extra functions or setup hooks. Next rounds: keep interface stable, coordinate with peers if needed.
